text:
You grade one workflow job of Rho-Bank's procedure library against an answer key. An answering
agent serves customers by following this job exactly, as it is shown below (its steps, conditions,
arguments, rules and the facts it asks for; the quotes behind them are not shown to the agent).
For each fact in the key, decide whether the job leads the agent to it; for each trap, decide
whether the job tells the agent to do it. Judge only what the job says, not what a good agent
would know without it.

Facts:
- right: a step, an argument or a rule leads the agent to the fact for every case the fact names.
- partly: it does for some of the cases the fact names and is silent on the others, or it says
  it so loosely that an agent following it could give another answer.
- missing: nothing in the job leads the agent to it; the agent would have to work it out alone.
- wrong: the job leads the agent to a different answer for at least one case the fact names, even
  if it is right for others.

Traps:
- present: a step, an argument or a rule tells the agent to do it, for some case.
- absent: nothing in the job does.

Then list the conflicts: two steps, arguments or rules that give the same case different
instructions, so an agent could follow either.

Job: pin_lock_investigation_protocol

 "info": [
  {
   "field": "identity_values",
   "about": "Any 2 of date of birth, email, phone number, address, checked against the records",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "To verify your identity, could you please provide two of the following: your date of birth, email, phone number, or address on file?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "locked_cards",
   "about": "Which debit cards or checking accounts the customer says are locked. Confirm them against the records, and look up every checking account.",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "Which of your Rho-Bank debit cards are being declined, and which one would you like to start with?",
   "may_hold_back": false
  },
  {
   "field": "decline_description",
   "about": "What the decline message said (PIN locked, incorrect PIN, unable to verify PIN) and where it happened",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "What message did you see when the card was declined, and where were you using it?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "decline_circumstances",
   "about": "The customer's own account of each locked card: where they were, roughly what time, and what amount they tried. Do not reveal the records first.",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "Can you tell me what happened when this card was locked? Where were you, roughly what time was it, and what amount were you trying to spend or withdraw?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {

   "about": "For each card: pin_locked, pin_lock_reason, pin_attempts_remaining, status, issue_reason, date_issued, daily_atm_limit, card_number_last_4, and prior PIN locks in the last 90 days",
   "from": "records",
   "ask": null,
   "may_hold_back": false
  },
  {
   "field": "declined_transactions",
   "about": "For each account: the transactions of type atm_withdrawal_declined or pos_declined, with city, time, amount and spacing; the successful transactions of the last 7 days; the usual ATM withdrawal; overdraft fees; and the balance",
   "from": "records",
   "ask": null,
   "may_hold_back": false
  },
  {
   "field": "customer_location_time_confirmation",
   "about": "Whether the customer was at the declined attempt's location and time",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "I see your card was locked after failed PIN attempts at [location from transaction]. Were you at that location? / These attempts occurred at [time]. Were you trying to use your card at that time?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "amount_confirmation",
   "about": "Whether the customer tried the declined amounts. Ask only when the amount-pattern flag scored.",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "The attempts were for [amount 1], then [amount 2], then [amount 3]. Do you remember trying those specific amounts?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "attempts_were_yours",
   "about": "For a medium score: whether the failed PIN attempts were the customer's own",
   "from": "customer",

   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "unrecognized_successful_transactions",
   "about": "For a card that cannot be unlocked: whether each successful transaction in the suspicious period was the customer's",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "I see a [amount] transaction at [merchant] on [date]. Was that yours?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "cannot_unlock_choice",
   "about": "For a card that cannot be unlocked: which offered option the customer wants",
   "from": "customer",
   "ask": "For your protection I can't unlock this card. I can close it and send a replacement with a new number, transfer you to our security team, or reset your PIN. Which would you like?",
   "may_hold_back": true
  },
  {
   "field": "transfer_accepted",
   "about": "Whether the customer wants a transfer to the security team, and whether now or after their other cards",

 "steps": [
  {
   "id": "identify",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Look up the customer with the name, email or user id they give. Ask for 2 of these: date of birth, email, phone, address. Compare the answers with the record.",
   "call": "get_user_information_by_name",
   "args": {
    "customer_name": "the customer's stated name (or use get_user_information_by_email / get_user_information_by_id with what they gave)"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "check_identity",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Confirm that at least 2 values match the record from identify. Share no card or account information until they do. If they still do not match after you ask again, tell the customer you cannot verify them and stop.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "identify"
   ],
   "after": [
    "identify"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "time",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Get the current time. Use it as the timestamp for the verification log, and as 'now' for the 90-day and age calculations below.",
   "call": "get_current_time",
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "check_identity"
   ],
   "if": "identity verified in check_identity"
  },
  {
   "id": "log_verif",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Log the verification record with the verified user's details and the time from the time step.",
   "call": "log_verification",
   "args": {
    "name": "verified user's name",
    "user_id": "verified user id",
    "address": "record address",
    "email": "record email",
    "phone_number": "record phone",
    "date_of_birth": "record DOB (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "time_verified": "time from get_current_time"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "check_identity"
   ],
   "after": [
    "time"
   ],
   "if": "identity verified in check_identity"
  },
  {
   "id": "accounts",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 with unlock_discoverable_agent_tool, then call it with call_discoverable_agent_tool. Note each account's account_id, account_type, account_class (tier), status, balance and date_opened.",
   "call": "get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847",
   "args": {
    "user_id": "the verified user"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "log_verif"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "cards",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock the tool, then call it once for each checking account. Read each card's card_id, card_number_last_4, status, issue_reason, date_issued, daily_atm_limit, pin_locked, pin_attempts_remaining, pin_lock_reason, prior lock history, fraud_alert_active and velocity_blocked. Call it only for checking accounts; if it replies that an account is not a checking account, skip that account.",
   "call": "get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "each checking account id from accounts"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "accounts"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "txns",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock the tool, then call it once for each account that has a locked card, to get the declined attempts and the recent successful activity.",
   "call": "get_bank_account_transactions_9173",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "each checking account with a locked card"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked = TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_which_card",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If several cards are affected, ask which one the customer wants to start with, and go through the cards in that order. If another card on the same account is also locked, investigate every locked card on that account before unlocking any (check_other_locked).",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "more than one of the customer's cards is declined or locked"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_circumstances",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, you may ask the customer what happened: where they were, roughly when, and what they tried. Never reveal the scoring. Score the card from the card data and the declined transactions in txns. The customer's answers change the score only through the Step 4 questions (ask_location, ask_time, ask_amount), which name the location, time and amounts from the records.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked TRUE and the customer has not yet described how it was locked"
  },
  {
   "id": "not_locked_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If pin_locked is FALSE but pin_attempts_remaining is low, tell the customer how many attempts remain before the card locks. If they forgot the PIN, offer a PIN reset (unlock_and_post_unlock_pin_reset).",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "the card's pin_locked is FALSE and pin_attempts_remaining is low"
  },
  {
   "id": "code_83_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For a CODE 83 decline (the PIN could not be verified because of a network problem), explain that the PIN was not wrong and advise the customer to retry. If it keeps failing, suggest a signature transaction, a different terminal or merchant, or waiting 10-15 minutes. If the card lookup shows pin_locked TRUE, the card still goes through this protocol before any unlock (triggers).",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "the decline was 'unable to verify PIN' (CODE 83)"
  },
  {
   "id": "triggers",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, check the automatic triggers first:\n- Security hold: a chat agent cannot unlock the card; offer the security-team transfer for it.\n- Another locked card on the same account: finish investigating all cards before any unlock, scoring each card on its own.\n- Any card on the account replaced with issue_reason 'stolen' in the last 90 days: enhanced verification is required.\nIf a trigger is present, follow its escalation path. Otherwise proceed to scoring.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "txns",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "check_security_hold",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, read pin_lock_reason. If it is 'security_hold', do not score or unlock the card. Offer to transfer the customer to the security team for that card, and keep handling the customer's other cards normally.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_transfer",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer accepts the offer, transfer with reason fraud_or_security_concern. In the summary, give the customer's issue and what was attempted: the card on security hold and what was done for the other cards. Ask the customer whether they want to go now or after their other cards are handled.",
   "call": "transfer_to_human_agents",
   "args": {
    "summary": "the card with pin_lock_reason security_hold needs security team review; outcomes for the customer's other cards",
    "reason": "fraud_or_security_concern"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' AND the customer accepts the transfer offer"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_declined",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer declines the transfer, acknowledge it and do not unlock the card. A security hold is an automatic escalation trigger, so follow the cannot-unlock path for that card: first check_unauthorized, then cannot_unlock_options. If unauthorized transactions are found, dispute them, close the card and order a replacement. If none are found, explain the security concern and offer closure and replacement, or a PIN reset. Do only what the customer accepts. You may tell the customer they can contact Rho-Bank later about the card.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' AND the customer declines the transfer"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_last",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "When the customer has a security-hold card and other locked cards, each card has its own outcome. Before making the security-hold transfer, ask the customer whether they want to finish their other cards first. If they want to go now, tell them which cards are still open.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold",
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_lock_reason 'security_hold' and the customer has other locked cards still to handle"
  },
  {
   "id": "check_other_locked",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If another card on the same account also has pin_locked TRUE, investigate and score every locked card on that account before unlocking any of them. Each card gets its own score and outcome.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "another card on the same account also has pin_locked TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "check_recent_stolen",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If any card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' with date_issued within 90 days before the time from get_current_time, the card needs enhanced verification (last 4 SSN plus a security question) before an unlock. No tool or document gives a way to perform it, so tell the customer the card needs enhanced verification. Then follow the escalation path for automatic triggers: check_unauthorized, then cannot_unlock_options.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "a card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' and date_issued within 90 days"
  },
  {
   "id": "score",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Score each card that has no security hold and no recent-stolen trigger, using all of the flags below. Never reveal the calculation.\n- A1: declined city vs the address city. Same city 0, other city in the same state 1, other state 2, other country 3.\n- A2: 2 locations 1, 3 or more 2.\n- A3: +1 if all successful transactions in the last 7 days were in the home city but the declines were elsewhere.\n- B1: hour of the attempt. 6AM-10PM 0, 10PM-12AM 1, 12-2AM 2, 2-6AM 3.\n- B2: last successful PIN use 7-30 days ago 1, more than 30 days ago 2.\n- B3: gap between attempts. 2-5 min 1, 1-2 min 2, under 1 min 3.\n- C1: decreasing amounts 2.\n- C2: all round hundreds 1.\n- C3: 2-5x the average ATM withdrawal 1, more than 5x 2.\n- C4: 80-100% of daily_atm_limit 1, attempts totalling more than the limit 2.\n- D1: prior locks in 90 days. 1, 2 or 3+ score 1, 2 or 3.\n- D2: card age 1-3 months 1, under 1 month 2.\n- D3: another card with a velocity block +1, with a fraud alert +2.\n- E1: account age 3-6 months 1, under 3 months 2.\n- E2: 1 overdraft 1, 2 or more 2.\n- E3: balance $50-100 1, under $50 2.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "txns",
    "accounts",
    "identify",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers",
    "check_security_hold",
    "check_other_locked",
    "check_recent_stolen"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason is not 'security_hold' and no card on the account was replaced with issue_reason 'stolen' in the last 90 days"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_location",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the score is 5 or higher and A1 (location mismatch) scored, ask: 'I see your card was locked after failed PIN attempts at [location from transaction]. Were you at that location?' If yes, remove the location flags and rescore. If no, keep the score and proceed with caution.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "score >= 5 and A1 Location Mismatch scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "foreign_location_denied",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the declines were in a different country (A1 = 3) and the customer says they were not there, keep the location flags. If the customer also answers the time question with 'I was asleep' or similar, the card is CRITICAL: do not unlock it. Go to check_unauthorized, then recommend closure and replacement (cannot_unlock_options). The customer still having the physical card does not change this.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location"
   ],
   "if": "A1 is a different country and the customer denies being at that location"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_time",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the score is 5 or higher and the time-of-day flag (B1) scored 2 or more, ask: 'These attempts occurred at [time]. Were you trying to use your card at that time?' If they confirm, remove the time flag. If they say they were asleep or similar, treat the card as CRITICAL (likely fraud).",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "score >= 5 and time-of-day flag (B1) >= 2"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_amount",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the score is 5 or higher and the amount-pattern flag (C1) scored, read back the attempted amounts and ask whether the customer remembers trying them. If they confirm, remove the flag. If they deny it or seem confused, keep it.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "score >= 5 and the amount pattern flag (C1) scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "velocity_flag_stays",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "B3 scores 3 when consecutive failed attempts are less than 1 minute apart. Step 4 has questions only for the location, amount-pattern and time-of-day flags, so no customer answer removes B3. A card with B3 = 3 has a single 3-point flag even when the customer confirms the attempts were theirs. Do not unlock it; escalate it as single_flag_escalation says. Explain the security concern without revealing the calculation.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "the card's consecutive failed attempts were less than 1 minute apart (B3 = 3)"
  },
  {
   "id": "medium_question",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For a final score of 5-7, ask: 'I see failed PIN attempts on your card. Were those attempts yours?' The card may be unlocked only after this question has been asked (unlock_handoff). If the customer says the attempts were not theirs, no passage decides what follows. Tell them so, and ask whether they still want the card unlocked or would rather reset the PIN because someone may know it. Do only what the customer accepts.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_location",
    "ask_amount"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount"
   ],
   "if": "the card's recalculated score is 5-7"
  },
  {
   "id": "decide",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Apply the thresholds to each card:\n- 0-4: unlock.\n- 5-7: unlock only after asking whether the attempts were the customer's.\n- 8-10: unlock only if the customer confirms the location and time and gives a satisfactory explanation.\n- 11-14: no unlock on this call.\n- 15+, or a customer who says they were asleep (or similar) at the time of an attempt: CRITICAL. Do not unlock; go to check_unauthorized, then recommend closure and replacement (cannot_unlock_options).\n- 3+ prior locks: PIN reset instead of an unlock.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount",
    "medium_question"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount",
    "medium_question"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {

## The answer key

- K1 (overnight_denial): declined attempts in another US state between 2 AM and 6 AM that the customer denies, saying she was asleep at home, make the card CRITICAL (likely fraud): it is not unlocked, whatever the total; the job reaches this for a different state, not only for a different country
- K2 (critical_outcome): a CRITICAL card with no successful unauthorized transaction is recommended for closure and replacement because fraud is suspected, and on the customer's yes it is closed and a replacement ordered for the same checking account (the closing and the order may run in the jobs this one names)
- K3 (suspicious_period): the suspicious period checked for successful unauthorized transactions is the window of the declined attempts the customer denies (from the first of them to now): successful transactions before it, her usual home-city activity, are not put to her as possibly unauthorized and not disputed, so a card whose period holds only declined attempts gets no dispute and she is told no money was taken
- K4 (admitted_attempts): a card whose declined attempts the customer confirms were hers (at that store, at that time, for that amount: she mixed up PINs) has its location flags removed and its score recalculated, and with no 3-point flag, fewer than 3 prior locks and a recalculated score of 10 or less it is cleared for unlock: not closed, not escalated, not sent to the cannot-unlock options
- K5 (card_order): locked cards on different checking accounts are taken one at a time, in the order the customer chooses, each to its outcome before the next is investigated; the trigger to finish investigating every locked card before any unlock applies only to locked cards on the same checking account
- K6 (two_prior_locks): a card cleared for unlock with 2 prior PIN locks in the last 90 days must be asked 'This is your third PIN lock in 90 days. Would you like me to reset your PIN to a new number?', and on a yes its PIN is reset to the new PIN the customer chooses (reset_debit_card_pin_6284, here or in the PIN-reset job this one names)
- K7 (security_hold): a card with pin_lock_reason security_hold is not scored, unlocked or reset: the agent offers a transfer to the security team, and when the customer declines it does nothing more on that card (no transfer, no write)

## The traps

- T1: every locked card the customer has, on any checking account, is investigated and scored before any of them is unlocked (the same-account trigger applied across accounts)
- T2: a PIN reset is offered, beside closure and a transfer, for a CRITICAL card (one whose overnight attempts the customer slept through); the reset clears the lock, so taking it unlocks a card that cannot be unlocked
- T4: the suspicious period reaches back before the first declined attempt the customer denies (to the last transaction she confirms as hers, or over the recent successful activity), so earlier home-city transactions she does not recognise are put to her and disputed
